subject: Re: Unexpected overnight embed unit spike — request for proof & sample logs
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@parcelflow.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Marco Li <marco.li@parcelflow.com>, ParcelFlow Billing <billing@parcelflow.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on July 6 overnight embed usage

Hi Lauren,

We reconciled our July 6 invoice and noticed ~1.2M embed units billed between 02:00–04:30 PDT. We did not run any large backfills or scheduled jobs during that window — our internal job scheduler shows only routine polling. Can you help explain the spike and provide raw request examples (request_id / timestamp / model / tokens_in / tokens_out) so we can match to our logs?

Attached is our billing summary and the line item in question. If this is a metering error, ParcelFlow will request a retroactive credit. Also, we need to understand whether EU VAT treatment is affected if any of that traffic is routed through our EU entity.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Director, Data Platform
ParcelFlow
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Anita Rao <anita@parcelflow.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on July 6 overnight embed usage

Anita — thanks for flagging this. I've looped in Ben (billing forensic) and Kim (metering infra). We'll pull the per-request IDs and a short evidence pack. Two quick asks to speed triage: 1) can you confirm whether the client used a single api key or multiple keys during July 5–7, and 2) do you have any internal job window identifiers (cron names / DAG ids) we should try to match?

We aim to get an initial sample file within 48 hours. Regarding VAT, if traffic originated from your EU entity we'll note it for the final credit calculation — Kim, can you include EU tax flagging in the export?

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Anita Rao <anita@parcelflow.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on July 6 overnight embed usage

Hi all,

We've started an extraction from the metering shard that covers 2027-07-05 20:00:00 UTC through 2027-07-07 06:00:00 UTC. Early finding: roughly 1.18M embed units show identical model and response-size distributions but are associated with two distinct request headers — one normal (api_key: pf-prod-01) and one showing a proxy health-check client (user_agent: cloud-probe/1.0). I'm attaching a small sample CSV (redwood-usage-samples-20270706.csv) with the columns: request_id, timestamp_utc, api_key_hash, model_name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, matched_customer_id.

Preliminary notes:
- We see a burst of short embedding requests (median prompt_tokens=6) that nevertheless spike unit counts due to a recent change in the embed unit multiplier for model rwd-embed-v2. We rolled out the multiplier fix on 2027-06-28; some old proxy clients that cached the previous multiplier may have retried requests.
- We don't yet have proof this originated from ParcelFlow's keys; the api_key_hash shown for the bulk spike does not match pf-prod-01, but cross-tenant collisions are rare.

Next steps:
1) Anita — if you can confirm any additional keys, we will run a deterministic hash match.
2) Vanessa — please prepare a short note on whether this pattern could arise from an upstream CDN probe or internal watchdog service.
3) Kim — include EU entity flags and raw headers in the expanded export.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Billing Forensics Analyst
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-usage-samples-20270706.csv (csv, 12KB)
From: Anita Rao <anita@parcelflow.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ParcelFlow Billing <billing@parcelflow.com>, Marco Li <marco.li@parcelflow.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on July 6 overnight embed usage

Thanks Ben — we pulled keys and verified pf-prod-01 was stationary. We do, however, have another key (pf-int-backup) that is rotated nightly by an internal watchdog. Marco confirmed the watcher does not initiate embed calls, but it does trigger a CDN-level probe that can invoke a thin API wrapper. Attached is a short schedule of our nightly maintenance windows.

Two requests from our side:
- Please run a hash match for pf-int-backup and include CDN/middleware user_agent strings in the evidence dump. If the request_ids map to pf-int-backup, ParcelFlow will accept a partial credit for the portion attributable to our housekeeping.
- If the culprit is an external probe (third-party CDN), we will need Redwood's recommended approach for preventing proxy-driven retries (rate-limits or 401 for probes). Also confirm whether VAT should be recalculated for any line-items after crediting.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — if you need anything else from our infra team I can loop them in.

Best,
Anita
